stem: CO2 has polar C=O bonds yet has no net dipole moment. This is because:

options.B: Its linear geometry causes the bond dipoles to cancel
options.C: Carbon and oxygen have equal electronegativities
options.D: The molecule is bent and the dipoles cancel

explanation: Correct: B) The two equal C=O bond dipoles point in opposite directions in a linear molecule, so the vector sum is zero. Why the others are wrong: A) Says the C=O bonds are nonpolar, but O is more electronegative than C so each bond is polar. C) Says C and O have equal electronegativities, which is false (O is 3.5, C is 2.5). D) Says CO2 is bent, but it is linear.
trap: Assuming polar bonds always yield a polar molecule.

stem: Which statement about SO2 is correct?

options.B: It is trigonal planar and nonpolar

explanation: Correct: C) Sulfur has two bonded oxygens and one lone pair (three electron domains), giving a bent shape with a net dipole. Why the others are wrong: A) Linear would require no lone pair and cannot be reached with three domains. B) Trigonal planar describes the electron geometry; the lone pair makes the molecular shape bent and polar. D) Tetrahedral would need four electron domains.
trap: Ignoring the lone pair when predicting molecular shape.

stem: Why is the H-O-H bond angle in water (about 104.5 degrees) smaller than the ideal tetrahedral angle of 109.5 degrees?

options.B: Hydrogen atoms repel each other more strongly than lone pairs do
options.D: Lone pair-bonding pair repulsion exceeds bonding pair-bonding pair repulsion

explanation: Correct: D) Lone pairs occupy more space, so lone pair-bonding pair repulsion exceeds bonding pair-bonding pair repulsion and compresses the angle below 109.5. Why the others are wrong: A) Says oxygen is sp2, but oxygen in water is approximately sp3. B) Says H atoms repel more than lone pairs, but lone pairs repel more than bonding pairs. C) Says oxygen has no lone pairs, but it has two.
trap: Counting only bonded atoms when deciding geometry.

stem: Ethanol (CH3CH2OH) boils at 78 C while dimethyl ether (CH3OCH3), its isomer, boils at about -24 C. The best explanation is:

options.A: Ethanol can hydrogen bond to itself, whereas dimethyl ether cannot
options.B: Ethanol has a higher molar mass
options.C: Dimethyl ether has stronger dispersion forces

explanation: Correct: A) Ethanol has an O-H group that serves as a hydrogen-bond donor, whereas the ether has no H on oxygen. Why the others are wrong: B) Cites higher molar mass, but the two are isomers with identical molar mass. C) Claims dimethyl ether has stronger dispersion forces, but they are comparable and cannot explain a 100 C gap. D) Claims dimethyl ether is nonpolar, but its bent C-O-C geometry makes it polar.
trap: Attributing the difference to molar mass when the compounds are isomers.

stem: Which has the lower boiling point, n-pentane or neopentane (2,2-dimethylpropane), and why?

options.A: n-Pentane, because it is more branched
options.B: Neopentane, because its compact shape reduces surface area for dispersion forces
options.C: Neopentane, because it has lower molar mass
options.D: They are equal because they are isomers

explanation: Correct: B) Branching lowers contact surface area, weakening London dispersion forces, so compact neopentane boils lower. Why the others are wrong: A) Says n-pentane is more branched, but n-pentane is the unbranched isomer. C) Says neopentane has lower molar mass, but both are C5H12 with identical mass. D) Says isomers have equal boiling points, but shape changes dispersion forces.
trap: Assuming isomers have the same physical properties.

stem: What is the hybridization of each carbon in ethyne (HC≡CH)?
explanation: Correct: C) Each carbon has two electron domains (one sigma bond to H, one to C), requiring sp hybrids; the two pi bonds use unhybridized p orbitals. Why the others are wrong: A) sp2 corresponds to three electron domains. B) sp3 corresponds to four electron domains. D) sp3d is not used for carbon.
trap: Counting bonds rather than electron domains.

stem: How many sigma and pi bonds are in acetonitrile, CH3-C≡N?
explanation: Correct: D) Three C-H sigma bonds, one C-C sigma bond and one C-N sigma bond give 5 sigma; the triple bond contains 2 pi bonds. Why the others are wrong: A) 4 sigma omits one sigma bond and 3 pi counts the triple bond as all pi. B) 3 sigma omits the C-C and C-N sigma bonds and 3 pi overcounts pi bonds. C) 5 sigma with 3 pi overcounts pi bonds; a triple bond has one sigma and two pi.
trap: Counting a triple bond as three pi bonds or forgetting the C-H bonds.

stem: Which ordering of carbon-carbon bonds is correct for bond length (longest to shortest)?
explanation: Correct: A) Higher bond order pulls the atoms closer, so C-C is longest, then C=C, then C≡C shortest. Why the others are wrong: B) Reverses the order, placing the triple bond longest. C) Places C=C longest and scrambles the bond-order ranking. D) Places the triple bond ahead of the double bond in length, contradicting bond order.
trap: Assuming stronger bonds are longer.

stem: Which bond is the most polar?
explanation: Correct: B) Polarity increases with electronegativity difference; F is the most electronegative partner (4.0 vs 2.5 for C). Why the others are wrong: A) C-O has a smaller difference since O (3.5) is less electronegative than F. C) C-N has a smaller difference since N (3.0) is less electronegative than F. D) C-Cl has a smaller difference since Cl (3.0) is less electronegative than F.
trap: Picking oxygen because it is common in biomolecules.

stem: What is the formal charge on oxygen in the hydronium ion, H3O+?
explanation: Correct: C) Oxygen has 3 bonds and 1 lone pair: 6 - 2 - 3 = +1. Why the others are wrong: A) 0 would require 2 bonds and 2 lone pairs, as in neutral water. B) -1 would need one bond and three lone pairs, as in hydroxide. D) +2 does not result from any valid count for this structure.
trap: Forgetting to count lone-pair electrons in formal charge.

stem: In the carbonate ion, CO3^2-, how do the three C-O bond lengths compare?

options.A: One is shorter than the other two
options.B: Two are single and one is double
options.D: All three are equal, intermediate between single and double bonds

explanation: Correct: D) Resonance delocalizes charge and double-bond character evenly over three equivalent oxygens (bond order about 1.33), so all C-O bonds are equal. Why the others are wrong: A) Says one bond is shorter, treating one resonance structure as real. B) Says two are single and one double, again treating a single Lewis structure as the real structure. C) Says all are single bonds, ignoring the partial double-bond character.
trap: Treating one resonance structure as the real structure.

stem: At the same temperature, which liquid has the highest vapor pressure?
explanation: Correct: A) Diethyl ether lacks hydrogen-bond donors and has weaker intermolecular forces, so more molecules escape to the vapor. Why the others are wrong: B) Ethanol is strongly hydrogen bonded, lowering its vapor pressure. C) Water is strongly hydrogen bonded, lowering its vapor pressure. D) Ethylene glycol has two OH groups and strong hydrogen bonding, giving very low vapor pressure.
trap: Linking higher molar mass with higher vapor pressure.

stem: Which solute is most soluble in hexane?
explanation: Correct: B) Hexane is nonpolar; nonpolar I2 dissolves through dispersion interactions (like dissolves like). Why the others are wrong: A) NaCl is ionic and does not interact favorably with hexane. C) Glucose is highly polar with many OH groups, so it is poorly soluble in hexane. D) KOH is ionic and insoluble in nonpolar hexane.
trap: Choosing based on molecular size instead of polarity.

stem: Which ranking of typical interaction strengths is correct, strongest to weakest?

options.A: London dispersion > hydrogen bond > ion-dipole > dipole-dipole
options.B: Dipole-dipole > ion-dipole > London dispersion > hydrogen bond
options.C: Ion-dipole > hydrogen bond > dipole-dipole > London dispersion (for comparable small molecules)
options.D: Hydrogen bond > London dispersion > ion-dipole > dipole-dipole

explanation: Correct: C) Charge-involving interactions are strongest, followed by hydrogen bonds, then permanent dipoles, then transient induced dipoles. Why the others are wrong: A) Places dispersion first and ion-dipole and dipole-dipole in reverse order. B) Places dipole-dipole first and hydrogen bonds last, which scrambles the order. D) Places hydrogen bond above ion-dipole and dispersion above dipole-dipole, both incorrect.
trap: Forgetting that ion-dipole interactions outrank hydrogen bonds.

stem: Which noble gas has the highest boiling point?
explanation: Correct: D) Larger atoms are more polarizable, so dispersion forces and boiling points increase down the group; Xe is the largest. Why the others are wrong: A) Neon has few electrons and weak induced dipoles. B) Helium has the fewest electrons and the lowest boiling point of all. C) Argon is more polarizable than Ne and He but less than Xe.
trap: Assuming heavier atoms have lower boiling points like in some other periodic trends.

stem: Which compound cannot act as a hydrogen-bond donor to itself?
explanation: Correct: A) Acetone has no H attached to O, N or F, so it can accept but not donate hydrogen bonds. Why the others are wrong: B) Ethanol has an O-H donor hydrogen. C) Acetic acid has an O-H donor hydrogen (and forms dimers). D) Methylamine has N-H donor hydrogens.
trap: Thinking any compound with an oxygen can donate hydrogen bonds.

stem: A DNA duplex rich in G-C pairs has a higher melting temperature than an A-T-rich duplex because:

options.B: G-C pairs share three hydrogen bonds, A-T pairs only two
options.D: G is a pyrimidine and A is a purine

explanation: Correct: B) G-C pairs share three hydrogen bonds versus two for A-T, and stack more strongly, so more energy is needed to separate the strands. Why the others are wrong: A) Says G-C pairs form covalent bonds, but base pairs are held by non-covalent hydrogen bonds. C) Says A-T pairs contain more phosphate, but phosphates are in the backbone, not the pairing. D) Says G is a pyrimidine and A a purine, but both are purines.
trap: Confusing hydrogen bond count between G-C and A-T.

stem: In an alpha helix, hydrogen bonds form between:

options.A: The side chains of adjacent residues only
options.B: Backbone atoms of residues on different strands
options.C: The backbone C=O of residue i and the backbone N-H of residue i+4

explanation: Correct: C) In an alpha helix the backbone C=O of residue i hydrogen bonds to the backbone N-H of residue i+4, parallel to the helix axis. Why the others are wrong: A) Says side chains of adjacent residues bond, but side chains are not the main source. B) Describes cross-strand backbone bonds, which are the pattern in beta sheets. D) Disulfides are covalent bonds, not hydrogen bonds.
trap: Mixing up alpha-helix and beta-sheet hydrogen bonding patterns.

stem: Why does NaCl have a much higher melting point than methane?

options.D: Strong electrostatic forces in the ionic lattice must be overcome

explanation: Correct: D) Strong Coulombic attractions in the ionic lattice must be overcome to melt NaCl, far stronger than dispersion forces between methane molecules. Why the others are wrong: A) Methane cannot hydrogen bond since it has no O-H, N-H or F-H. B) NaCl does not owe its melting point to dispersion forces; its ionic attractions are much stronger. C) Methane is a molecular solid, not a covalent network.
trap: Thinking covalent bonds within methane must break on melting.

stem: Compressing ice at a temperature slightly below 0 C can cause it to melt. Which feature of the phase diagram explains this?

options.A: The solid-liquid boundary has a negative slope
options.B: The triple point lies at high pressure
options.C: The critical point is above 100 C

explanation: Correct: A) Because ice is less dense than water, increased pressure favors the liquid, so the solid-liquid boundary slopes backward (negative slope). Why the others are wrong: B) The triple point location does not explain melting under compression. C) The critical point concerns liquid-gas behavior, not ice melting under pressure. D) Sublimation curves slope upward, not horizontally, and relate to solid-gas transition.
trap: Assuming the solid-liquid line always slopes positively.

stem: A solution has a solvent mole fraction of 0.80, and the pure solvent has vapor pressure 100 torr. Assuming ideal behavior, what is the solvent vapor pressure above the solution?
explanation: Correct: B) Raoult's law gives P = X(solvent) x P° = 0.80 x 100 = 80 torr. Why the others are wrong: A) 20 torr uses the solute mole fraction instead of the solvent's. C) 125 torr inverts the relation by dividing by 0.80. D) 100 torr ignores the dissolved solute, which lowers vapor pressure.
trap: Using solute mole fraction in Raoult's law.

stem: Which statement about 1,2-dichloroethene is correct?

options.A: The trans isomer is polar and has the higher boiling point
options.C: The cis isomer is polar and has the higher boiling point
options.D: Both isomers have identical dipole moments

explanation: Correct: C) In the cis isomer the C-Cl dipoles add; in the trans isomer they cancel, so dipole-dipole forces raise the cis boiling point. Why the others are wrong: A) Says trans is polar, but the trans isomer has zero net dipole. B) Says both are nonpolar, but both contain polar C-Cl bonds and cis has a net dipole. D) Says dipole moments are identical, but cis has a net dipole and trans has none.
trap: Assuming the symmetric trans isomer must be the polar one, or that both isomers behave identically because they have the same bonds.

stem: The nitrogen in an amide is planar rather than pyramidal because:

options.C: Hydrogen bonding forces it to flatten
options.D: Resonance delocalizes its lone pair into the carbonyl, giving partial double-bond character

explanation: Correct: D) Resonance delocalizes the N lone pair into the carbonyl, giving partial C-N double-bond character, planar geometry and restricted rotation. Why the others are wrong: A) Says N has no lone pair, but it does, and that lone pair is what delocalizes. B) Says N is sp3, but a localized sp3 nitrogen would be pyramidal. C) Says hydrogen bonding flattens N, but the planarity arises from resonance.
trap: Assuming nitrogen always remains sp3.

stem: Using bond energies (H-H 436, Cl-Cl 243, H-Cl 431 kJ/mol), what is the estimated delta H for H2 + Cl2 -> 2 HCl?
explanation: Correct: A) delta H = bonds broken - bonds formed = (436 + 243) - 2(431) = 679 - 862 = -183 kJ/mol. Why the others are wrong: B) +183 reverses the sign by subtracting broken from formed. C) -862 counts only the bonds formed. D) +679 counts only the bonds broken.
trap: Reversing bonds broken and formed.

stem: Which molecule contains a central atom with an expanded octet?
explanation: Correct: B) Sulfur, a third-period element, can accommodate 12 electrons around it in SF6, an expanded octet. Why the others are wrong: A) Carbon in CF4 has 8 electrons and obeys the octet. C) Nitrogen in NF3 has 8 electrons and is a second-period atom. D) Oxygen in OF2 has 8 electrons and is a second-period atom.
trap: Applying the octet rule to third-period atoms.

stem: Which molecule is polar?
explanation: Correct: C) CHCl3 has asymmetric bond dipoles (C-H and C-Cl differ) that do not cancel, giving a net dipole. Why the others are wrong: A) CCl4 is symmetric tetrahedral, so its C-Cl dipoles cancel. B) CH4 is symmetric tetrahedral with nearly nonpolar bonds. D) CF4 is symmetric tetrahedral, so its C-F dipoles cancel.
trap: Judging polarity only from the presence of polar bonds.

stem: In a soluble globular protein, nonpolar side chains are typically found:

options.A: On the surface exposed to water
options.D: In the interior, away from water

explanation: Correct: D) Burying nonpolar side chains minimizes unfavorable contact with water, driving folding (hydrophobic effect). Why the others are wrong: A) Says they sit on the surface, but surface residues are mostly polar or charged. B) Says they appear only at the N-terminus, but location is not terminus-dependent. C) Says they appear only in disulfides, but disulfides involve cysteine only.
trap: Reversing the pattern for membrane versus soluble proteins.

stem: What are the bond angles in PCl5, which has trigonal bipyramidal geometry?
explanation: Correct: A) In trigonal bipyramidal geometry axial-equatorial angles are 90 degrees and equatorial-equatorial angles are 120 degrees. Why the others are wrong: B) 109.5 describes tetrahedral geometry. C) 180 degrees alone describes a linear arrangement (axial-axial is only one of the angles). D) 90 only describes octahedral-like angles, missing the 120 degree equatorial angles.
trap: Using a single ideal angle for all five-domain geometries.

stem: At room temperature Br2 is a liquid while Cl2 is a gas. The best explanation is:

options.B: Br2 is larger and more polarizable, giving stronger dispersion forces
options.C: Br2 has a larger permanent dipole
options.D: Br2 has a stronger covalent bond than Cl2

explanation: Correct: B) Br2 is larger and more polarizable, so its dispersion forces are stronger, making it liquid at room temperature. Why the others are wrong: A) Says Br2 hydrogen bonds, but it has no H on N, O or F. C) Says Br2 has a permanent dipole, but homonuclear diatomics are nonpolar. D) Cites stronger covalent bond, but vaporization overcomes intermolecular forces, and the Br-Br bond is actually weaker.
trap: Attributing physical state to bond strength or permanent dipoles.

stem: Which ordering of boiling points (lowest to highest) is correct for butane, propanal and 1-propanol?
explanation: Correct: C) Butane has only dispersion forces, propanal adds dipole-dipole, and 1-propanol hydrogen bonds, giving the highest boiling point. Why the others are wrong: A) Puts propanal below butane, ignoring propanal's dipole-dipole attractions. B) Reverses the order, placing hydrogen-bonding 1-propanol lowest. D) Places 1-propanol below propanal, underestimating hydrogen bonding.
trap: Ignoring forces when molar masses are similar.

stem: Which diatomic molecule has the highest bond dissociation energy?
explanation: Correct: D) The triple bond of N2 (about 945 kJ/mol) is very strong. Why the others are wrong: A) O2 has only a double bond. B) F2 has only a weak single bond. C) Cl2 has only a single bond.
trap: Choosing based on atomic size.

stem: Which statement describes the formation of NH4+ from NH3 and H+?

options.A: Nitrogen donates its lone pair to H+, forming a coordinate covalent bond
options.B: Hydrogen donates an electron pair to nitrogen
options.C: An ionic bond forms between N and H+
options.D: Nitrogen loses an electron to hydrogen

explanation: Correct: A) A lone pair on N is shared with the proton, forming a coordinate covalent bond; all four N-H bonds are then equivalent. Why the others are wrong: B) Says hydrogen donates a pair, but H+ has no electrons to donate. C) Says an ionic bond forms, but the bond is covalent. D) Says nitrogen loses an electron to hydrogen, but no electron transfer occurs.
trap: Reversing the role of Lewis acid and Lewis base.

stem: Which ionic compound has the larger lattice energy, MgO or NaCl?

options.A: NaCl, because it has a larger ion
options.B: MgO, because the ions have higher charges
options.C: NaCl, because Na+ is a smaller ion

explanation: Correct: B) Lattice energy scales with the product of charges (2+/2- vs 1+/1-) and inversely with ion separation, so MgO is much larger. Why the others are wrong: A) Says NaCl is larger because of a larger ion, but larger ions lower lattice energy. C) Says NaCl is larger because Na+ is smaller, ignoring that MgO ions are even smaller and more highly charged. D) Says they are equal, but the charges differ.
trap: Focusing on radius alone while ignoring charge.

stem: Why does water boil at a lower temperature at high altitude?

options.A: The covalent bonds in water are weaker
options.B: Water has fewer hydrogen bonds at altitude
options.C: Boiling occurs when vapor pressure equals the lower external pressure
options.D: Water has a lower specific heat at altitude

explanation: Correct: C) Boiling occurs when vapor pressure equals external pressure; at altitude the external pressure is lower, so boiling occurs at a lower temperature. Why the others are wrong: A) Says covalent bonds weaken, but altitude does not change O-H bond strength. B) Says fewer hydrogen bonds at altitude, but hydrogen bonding depends on temperature, not altitude. D) Says specific heat is lower at altitude, but specific heat is unaffected.
trap: Treating boiling as a function of bond strength.

stem: o-Nitrophenol has a lower boiling point than p-nitrophenol. This is best explained by:

options.A: Greater molar mass of the para isomer
options.B: Weaker covalent bonds in the ortho isomer
options.C: Absence of an -OH group in the ortho isomer
options.D: Intramolecular hydrogen bonding in the ortho isomer reduces intermolecular attractions

explanation: Correct: D) Intramolecular hydrogen bonding in the ortho isomer leaves fewer groups free to bond between molecules, lowering the boiling point. Why the others are wrong: A) Says the para isomer has greater mass, but the isomers have equal mass. B) Says covalent bonds are weaker in ortho, but covalent strength is not what is overcome in boiling. C) Says ortho lacks an OH group, but both isomers have the same groups.
trap: Assuming all hydrogen bonding raises boiling point.

stem: A dipole consists of charges +q and -q separated by distance d. If d doubles while q remains the same, the dipole moment:
explanation: Correct: A) Dipole moment mu = q x d, so doubling d doubles mu. Why the others are wrong: B) Halving would require an inverse relationship, which does not apply. C) Quadrupling would require a quadratic dependence on d. D) Staying unchanged ignores that mu depends linearly on separation.
trap: Misapplying inverse-square relationships from Coulomb's law.

stem: Which is the largest ion among O2-, F-, Na+ and Mg2+?
explanation: Correct: B) These ions are isoelectronic (10 electrons); O2- has the fewest protons (8), the weakest nuclear pull, and the largest radius. Why the others are wrong: A) F- has 9 protons, so it is pulled in more than O2-. C) Na+ has 11 protons, pulling the same 10 electrons more tightly. D) Mg2+ has 12 protons and is the smallest of the group.
trap: Assuming anions are always larger than cations of the next period without comparing protons.

stem: Rotation about a carbon-carbon double bond is restricted because:

options.B: The double bond is longer than a single bond
options.C: Rotation would break the overlap of the pi bond

explanation: Correct: C) Pi overlap between parallel p orbitals is lost on twisting 90 degrees, so rotation is restricted and cis/trans isomers are stable. Why the others are wrong: A) Says sigma bonds cannot rotate, but sigma bonds rotate freely. B) Says double bonds are longer, but they are shorter, and length does not cause the restriction. D) Says hydrogen bonding locks it, which has nothing to do with alkene rotation.
trap: Believing sigma bonds restrict rotation.

stem: Which molecule is trigonal planar?
explanation: Correct: D) Boron in BF3 has three bonding domains and no lone pair, giving trigonal planar geometry. Why the others are wrong: A) NF3 has a lone pair on N, giving trigonal pyramidal shape. B) PCl3 has a lone pair on P, giving trigonal pyramidal shape. C) NH3 has a lone pair on N, giving trigonal pyramidal shape.
trap: Ignoring lone pairs on central atoms.

stem: In the reaction BF3 + NH3 -> F3B-NH3, which species is the Lewis acid?

options.A: BF3, which accepts an electron pair
options.B: NH3, which accepts an electron pair
options.C: BF3, which donates an electron pair

explanation: Correct: A) Boron in BF3 has an incomplete octet and accepts the nitrogen lone pair, so BF3 is the Lewis acid. Why the others are wrong: B) Says NH3 accepts a pair, but NH3 donates its lone pair and is the Lewis base. C) Says BF3 donates a pair, but it accepts one. D) Says NH3 donates a proton, but no proton transfer occurs here.
trap: Confusing Lewis definitions with Bronsted definitions.
